_comment: Hand-written text for each language. Speaker numbers and countries come from data/languages.json (Unicode CLDR with World Bank populations), refreshed monthly.

languages.s: A Germanic language that began in early medieval England and is now used on every continent as a first, second or shared language.
languages.fun: English has borrowed words from many languages. Pajamas came from Hindi and Urdu, robot from Czech, and ketchup from a Chinese word.
languages.special: More people use English as a second language than as a first language.

languages.s: A family of closely related languages, led by Mandarin, written with characters that have been in use for over 3,000 years.
languages.fun: Mandarin, Cantonese, Wu and other varieties share one writing system, but when spoken they are often not understood by each other's speakers.
languages.special: Chinese characters stand for meanings as well as sounds, so people who speak different varieties can read the same text.

languages.s: One of the main languages of India, written in the Devanagari script and widely understood across South Asia.
languages.fun: Hindi and Urdu sound almost the same in everyday speech, but they are written in different scripts.
languages.special: English borrowed words such as jungle, shampoo and bungalow from Hindi and nearby languages of India.

languages.s: A Romance language that grew from Latin in medieval Spain and spread to the Americas, Africa and Asia.
languages.fun: Spanish writes an upside-down question mark at the start of a question, so the reader knows how to read the sentence from its first word.
languages.special: Spanish is an official language in about 20 countries, from Mexico to Argentina and from Spain to Equatorial Guinea.

languages.script: Arabic script, written right to left
languages.s: The language of the Quran and of more than twenty countries, with many spoken dialects and one shared formal version.
languages.fun: Spoken Arabic differs a lot from place to place, so news and books use a shared formal version called Modern Standard Arabic.
languages.special: English words such as coffee, sugar and algebra came from Arabic.

languages.s: A Romance language from France that is an official language in many countries across Europe, Africa, the Americas and the Pacific.
languages.fun: In France, 70 is said as sixty-ten (soixante-dix) and 80 as four twenties (quatre-vingts).
languages.special: French is one of the six official languages of the United Nations and was the main language of diplomacy for centuries.

languages.s: The national language of Pakistan and one of the official languages of India, rich in poetry.
languages.fun: The word Urdu comes from a Turkic word for an army camp, ordu.
languages.special: Urdu is often written in Nastaliq, a flowing style of calligraphy.

languages.s: The language of Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal, with a strong literary tradition.
languages.fun: The Language Movement of 21 February 1952 in Bangladesh led UNESCO to proclaim International Mother Language Day, held each year on 21 February.
languages.special: Rabindranath Tagore, who wrote in Bengali, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913. He was the first person outside Europe to win it.

languages.s: A Romance language that began in the west of the Iberian Peninsula and is now spoken on four continents.
languages.fun: Portuguese has the word saudade, for a deep, affectionate longing for something or someone far away.
languages.special: Portuguese is an official language in nine countries, including Brazil, Angola and Mozambique.

languages.s: The language of the Punjab region, which lies across India and Pakistan.
languages.fun: Punjabi is written in two scripts: Gurmukhi in India and Shahmukhi in Pakistan.
languages.special: Punjabi is a tonal language, which is unusual for a member of the Indo-European family.

languages.s: The most widely spoken Slavic language, used across Russia and many nearby countries.
languages.fun: Russian has no words for a or the, and in the present tense it usually leaves out the word is.
languages.special: Russian is one of the six official languages of the United Nations.

languages.s: A Bantu language used as a shared language across East Africa.
languages.fun: The word safari came into English through Swahili, and it comes from an Arabic word that means journey.
languages.special: Swahili is an official language of the African Union as well as of Tanzania and Kenya.

languages.s: The national language of Indonesia, a form of Malay used by people from hundreds of ethnic groups.
languages.fun: In 1928, Indonesian youth groups pledged to use one language, which helped make it the shared national language.
languages.special: Plurals are often made by repeating the word. Buku is a book and buku-buku is books.

languages.s: A Germanic language spoken in Germany, Austria, Switzerland and parts of nearby countries.
languages.fun: German writes every noun with a capital letter and can join words into very long compounds, such as Donaudampfschifffahrtsgesellschaft.
languages.special: German is the most widely spoken first language in the European Union.

languages.s: The language of Japan, written with three scripts that are often used in the same sentence.
languages.fun: Japanese is written with kanji, hiragana and katakana, all in the same text.
languages.special: Japanese has many levels of politeness, so the words and verb forms change with who is being spoken to.

languages.s: A Dravidian language spoken mainly in the Indian states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
languages.fun: Telugu has been called the Italian of the East because so many of its words end in vowels.
languages.special: Telugu is one of the classical languages of India.

languages.s: The language of the Indian state of Maharashtra, whose capital is Mumbai.
languages.fun: Marathi was officially named a classical language of India in 2024.
languages.special: Marathi is written in Devanagari, the same script used for Hindi.

languages.s: A language with more than a thousand years of poetry, spoken in Iran as Farsi, in Afghanistan as Dari and in Tajikistan as Tajik.
languages.fun: Verses by Persian poets such as Rumi and Hafez are still quoted in everyday conversation.
languages.special: The same language has three names: Farsi in Iran, Dari in Afghanistan and Tajik in Tajikistan.

languages.s: A Dravidian language of southern India and Sri Lanka with a literature that goes back over 2,000 years.
languages.fun: Tamil is one of the oldest classical languages still used in everyday life.
languages.special: Tamil is an official language in India, Sri Lanka and Singapore.

languages.s: The language of Vietnam, with six tones that are shown by marks on the letters.
languages.fun: Vietnamese uses the Latin alphabet with extra marks that show its six tones.
languages.special: The Latin-based script was shaped by European missionaries in the 1600s and later became the national script.

languages.s: The language of Turkey, which adds endings to a root word to build meaning.
languages.fun: In Turkish, one long word with added endings can say what takes a whole sentence in English.
languages.special: Turkey changed from the Arabic script to the Latin alphabet in 1928.

languages.s: The language of Korea, written in Hangul, a script designed to be easy to learn.
languages.fun: Hangul was created in the 1440s under King Sejong the Great so that ordinary people could learn to read.
languages.special: Hangul Day is celebrated every year on 9 October in South Korea.

languages.s: A Romance language that grew from Latin and is spoken in Italy, Switzerland, San Marino and Vatican City.
languages.fun: Many music terms used around the world, such as piano, forte and allegro, are Italian words.
languages.special: Modern standard Italian grew largely from the Tuscan dialect that Dante used in the Divine Comedy.

languages.s: The language of Thailand, with five tones and its own script.
languages.fun: Thai is a tonal language with five tones, and it is written without spaces between words.
languages.special: Tradition credits King Ramkhamhaeng with creating the Thai script in 1283.

languages.s: The main language of the Pashtun people in Afghanistan and Pakistan.
languages.fun: Pashto has a strong tradition of oral poetry, much of it passed on by voice.
languages.special: Pashto is an official language of Afghanistan, along with Dari.

languages.s: The national language of Ukraine, with a long tradition of folk songs and poetry.
languages.fun: The Ukrainian folk song Shchedryk became the carol known around the world as Carol of the Bells.
languages.special: Ukrainian is the only state language of Ukraine.

languages.s: The language of Poland, known for its long runs of consonants.
languages.fun: Polish has famously hard consonant clusters, as in the town name Szczebrzeszyn.
languages.special: Polish nouns change across seven cases.

languages.s: The language of the Netherlands and much of Belgium, where it is called Flemish.
languages.fun: The English words cookie, yacht and boss all came from Dutch.
languages.special: Dutch is an official language in the Netherlands, Belgium, Suriname and several Caribbean islands.

languages.s: A trade language across West Africa, spoken mainly in northern Nigeria and Niger.
languages.fun: Hausa was written for centuries in an Arabic-based script called Ajami before the Latin alphabet became common.
languages.special: Hausa is one of the most widely used languages in West Africa.

languages.s: The language of the Yoruba people of Nigeria, Benin and Togo.
languages.fun: Yoruba is a tonal language, so the same spelling can mean different things depending on the pitch.
languages.special: Yoruba is also used in religious traditions in the Americas, such as in Cuba and Brazil.

languages.s: The working language of the Ethiopian government.
languages.fun: Amharic is written in the Ge'ez script, in which each symbol stands for a consonant and a vowel together.
languages.special: Amharic is a Semitic language, closely related to Hebrew and Arabic.

languages.s: A language of Malaysia, Brunei, Singapore and Indonesia that served for centuries as the shared trading language of Southeast Asia.
languages.fun: The English word orangutan comes from Malay and means person of the forest.
languages.special: Indonesian is a close relative of Malay and is based on it.

languages.s: The national language of the Philippines, based on Tagalog.
languages.fun: Filipino has borrowed many words from Spanish and English.
languages.special: Filipino and English are both official languages of the Philippines.
